mission_05: Quantum feature maps encode classical data into quantum states, creating representations in exponentially large Hilbert spaces. Different encoding strategies offer trade-offs: angle encoding uses one qubit per feature with rotation gates (efficient but limited expressivity), amplitude encoding stores n features in log(n) qubits (exponentially compact but requires state preparation), and IQP (Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial) encoding uses Hadamard layers, RZ rotations, and entangling ZZ interactions to create highly expressive feature maps. The quality of a feature map is measured by how well it separates different data points (low overlap for different classes) while maintaining structure (high overlap for similar points). In this mission, you implement three encoding strategies, compute state overlaps as kernel values, and analyze feature space properties including effective dimension and pairwise overlaps.
